decisions.reason: As a close-to-core carpet launch in a growing furniture market, it is still early and inexpensive enough to keep this option open while the firm learns about customer response.

This hand-knotted wool silk carpet fits the firm's design-led premium positioning, and with no clear negative signal yet the option value of staying in the market outweighs the likely modest carrying cost.
Because it is another adjacent carpet offer within an already broad assortment, the firm would likely retain it for another period to test demand before making an irreversible exit.

The corner bench builds directly on the firm's established furniture capabilities, so keeping it on the market preserves a promising option in flexible living and workplace concepts under still-high uncertainty.
Even with overlap in carpets, this launch is close to the existing offer and likely cheap to maintain, so management would keep it until market feedback becomes more conclusive.
A swivel shell chair aligns well with the firm's residential and workplace business, and absent evidence of weak uptake the prudent real-options choice is to continue and observe.
